coverage: partial: findings recalled from the three reports, not extracted from their text; each row carries confidence

finding: commodity tracking: FEMA could not track ice, water and MRE shipments; total asset visibility system not in place at the scale required
ice shipments routed to staging areas far from the affected region and held for weeks (contracted trucks waiting)
pre-positioned commodities insufficient for the scale of the event; supply chain sized for smaller disasters
requests for commodities passed through multiple hands (state to FEMA to contractor) without a single record of the order state
evacuation bus commitment (contracted buses) arrived days late; commitment status not visible to the requesting parish
no-bid and expedited contracts with weak documentation of delivery
communications infrastructure destroyed across the coast; first responders unable to communicate for days
Superdome and Convention Center: commodities and evacuation held up by absent situational awareness of who was where and in what condition
Hurricane Pam exercise (2004) findings not converted into resourced plans before the event

finding: unsolicited and unregistered donations and volunteers could not be received or tracked
